title: cost: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Automated defaults for batching/caching and quantization profiles improve cost efficiency without impacting latency SLOs. Adds unit-econ tool to surface per-route cost drivers.
description:
Motivation: Customers consistently ask for turnkey cost savings that don't require deep runtime tuning. This PR implements an automated defaults/autotune path for batching and prefix/KV caching, ships model quantization profiles for common families, and adds a small unit-economics toolkit to the Console to make cost tradeoffs visible.

What this changes: - Autotune controller that adjusts batch sizes and batching windows per-route using recent latency and throughput signals. - Default prefix/KV cache TTLs and cache admission heuristics based on request patterns. - Quantization profile catalog (INT8/FP16 suggestions) and an API for model-level recommended profile. - Unit-econ tooling: per-route token cost breakdown, expected cost delta for changing batch/cache/quant settings, and an API endpoint to run simulation scenarios.

Backwards compatibility: All changes are opt-in by default at the tenant level. The autotune controller can be enabled via config flags; quant suggestions do not change served model weights automatically.

Testing & validation: - Microbenchmarks on p3/rtx fleets for 8 representative models (gpt-like, opt, llama variants). - End-to-end canary run on staging with 10% traffic for 72h. - Unit + integration tests for the controller and Console UI.

Rollout plan: - Stage rollout to Dedicated customers with opt-in flag, monitor latency p50/p99 and error rate. - Gradual enable via feature flags and telemetry thresholds.

Related: Linear ENG-2315 (autotune ranking), ENG-2490 (quant profiles), SUP-512 (customer request to reduce inference unit cost).

ci_checks: CI: e2e(canary) — passed on staging after 72h
CI: perf-bench (pre-merge) — initial runs showed a 15-22% cost reduction across sample routes
benchmarks: Sample results (p3.2xlarge, 8 models): cost/unit tokens reduced by 18% median, p50 latency unchanged, p99 improved slightly for batched workloads.
KV cache hit ratio improved by 12% for workloads with repeated prefixes after admission heuristics applied.
Quant profile simulation: INT8 profiles reduced per-token GPU time by ~10% for eligible models with negligible quality impact on eval prompts.
testing_notes: Staging canary (10% traffic, 72h): no increase in error rate; p99 latency within 5% of baseline for all routes.
Synthetic load tests validated controller stability under rapid traffic spikes.
Added unit tests covering estimator edge-cases and quant profile parsing.
